definitions.gloss: one serving; one portion (for one person)
definitions.explanation: Used when ordering or describing food quantities.
Describes someone who has become competent or grown into a capable adult.

examples.japanese: ラーメン{一人前|いちにんまえ}ください。
{料理|りょうり}は{二人前|ふたりまえ}{頼|たの}みましょう。
examples.english: Let's order two servings of the dish.

examples.japanese: {一人前|いちにんまえ}の{量|りょう}が{多|おお}すぎて{食|た}べきれなかった。
examples.english: One serving was too much and I couldn't finish it.

examples.japanese: そばを{三人前|さんにんまえ}{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
examples.english: I ordered three servings of soba.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{量|りょう}がとても{多|おお}いので、{二人|ふたり}で{一人前|いちにんまえ}を{分|わ}けて{食|た}べた。
examples.english: This restaurant's servings are very large, so two of us split one serving.

examples.japanese: {一人前|いちにんまえ}になりたい。
examples.english: I want to become a full-fledged adult.

examples.japanese: やっと{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{社会人|しゃかいじん}になれた。
examples.english: I've finally become a full-fledged member of society.

examples.japanese: まだ{半人前|はんにんまえ}だけど、いつか{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{職人|しょくにん}になりたい。
examples.english: I'm still only half-qualified, but someday I want to become a fully-fledged craftsman.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どものくせに{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{口|くち}を{利|き}くな。
examples.english: Don't talk like a grown-up when you're just a child.
examples.notes: {一人前|いちにんまえ}の{口|くち}を{利|き}く is a set expression meaning to speak as if one were a competent adult.

examples.japanese: {十年|じゅうねん}{修行|しゅぎょう}して、やっと{一人前|いちにんまえ}と{認|みと}められた。
examples.english: After ten years of training, I was finally recognized as fully qualified.

notes:
{一人前|いちにんまえ} has two related meanings.

SENSE 1 - FOOD PORTIONS:
・{一人前|いちにんまえ} - one serving
・{二人前|ふたりまえ} - two servings
・{三人前|さんにんまえ} - three servings

SENSE 2 - FULLY QUALIFIED:
・{一人前|いちにんまえ}になる - to become full-fledged
・{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{職人|しょくにん} - a fully qualified craftsman
・まだ{半人前|はんにんまえ} - still only half-qualified

EXPRESSION:
・{一人前|いちにんまえ}の{口|くち}を{利|き}く - to talk like a grown-up
